title: The pro-etale multiplication-difference criterion
statement: Let $X$ be any scheme and let $O$ be any sheaf of commutative rings on the coefficient-sized small pro-etale model [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For any object $U$, section $f\in O(U)$, and module sheaves on its slice [def-pur-localized-ringed-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], let $P$ and $\Delta_f$ be as in [def-weil-pbc-multiplication-difference]. Then $P$ is exact. Use the standard derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the genuine sheafified sectionwise localization $O|_U[1/f]$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization], and derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For any module sheaf F on the ambient site, after restricting F to the slice, $R\mathcal Hom(O|_U[1/f],F[0])=0$ if and only if $\Delta_f(F)$ is invertible. For any cochain complex K of module sheaves on the ambient site, after termwise restriction to the slice, invertibility of every $\Delta_f(K^i)$ implies $R\mathcal Hom(O|_U[1/f],Q(K))=0$. No boundedness, finiteness or ideal hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Transport the coefficient-sized slice to the raw pro-etale slice by Over.postEquiv for AsSmall.down. The weakly-etale slice equivalence then identifies it with the pro-etale site of the underlying scheme. The ring-sheaf comparison induces the actual module equivalence by pushforwardPushforwardEquivalence. The proved exact_countable_products helper of ProEtaleSurjectiveTowerDerivedLimit packages countableProducts_exact, and exact products transport back along the equivalence. Powers preserve homology because the diagonal and product functors preserve finite limits and finite colimits.

Compare localSectionMultiplication on the unit module with the map specified by unitHomEquiv, using commutativity. scalarLocalization_regularColimit identifies the telescope colimit with actual sectionwise localization. For an ambient derived object, choose a derived-limit witness by exists_isDerivedLimit_and_iso. The existing local Hom/tower criterion and the distinguished triangle zero/isomorphism equivalence identify Hom vanishing with invertibility of the tower endomorphism. Conjugate along mapDerivedCategoryFactors to the image of a complex tower. The exact-product theorem identifies the derived product with the image of the termwise product. Check the tower comparison after every product projection.

For degree-zero objects, multiplication commutes with the single-complex/restriction comparison, checked in degree zero. The single derived functor preserves countable products by the exact-product theorem; its full faithfulness reflects invertibility. Hence derived tower invertibility is equivalent to the ordinary module difference being invertible. For a general ambient complex, evaluation preserves the product and commutes with the tower endomorphism. Invertible component differences therefore give a chain isomorphism. Its image in the derived category is invertible, so the local Hom/tower criterion gives vanishing after the localization and restriction comparisons.
